findings.baldosa: The pinned Baldosa guest (product integration target, snesrecomp fork 075fbe4) matches the references within one frame on all five attract-cycle loads (black runs 248-276, 401-443, 941-1097, 1422-1547, 3632-3761 vs bsnes 248-276, 401-443, 941-1098, 1423-1547, 3632-3762) and completes 1327 vblank-wait passes (Beetle 1327, Snes9x 1326; legacy-pin native 1311). The RF-014 load deficit is specific to the legacy snesrecomp pin cd5875c.
findings.blank_screens: Every frontend load keeps the screen black longer on native than on the high-accuracy bsnes core (Snes9x and Beetle agree within one frame): stock 2P route +2, +3, +1 frames; attract cycle +2, +3, +3, +2 with native's later loads starting 17 frames late by host 3632; 2P race-finish transition +1. A generic SNESRecomp build gives +2, +3, 0 on the stock route. The first load (host 248-276 on the reference) is a CPU-bound decompress-to-VRAM routine (bank 81 unrolled STA $2118 at 81:CD70-81:D09C) during which WRAM at $0200+ is byte-identical between native and Snes9x.
findings.census: 10,400 of 10,400 signed native frontier cases replayed on Snes9x at L=2: 10,378 coarse agreement, 22 census-attribution-ambiguous (token owned by an earlier case), 0 coarse divergence
findings.lag_frames: 7E:00C6 vblank-wait passes: stock 2P route host 2-1126 native 773, Snes9x 801, Beetle-bsnes 802; no-input attract cycle host 2-4002 (one rewrite window excluded) native 1311, Snes9x 1326, Beetle-bsnes 1327; generic SNESRecomp native (stock route) 772
findings.mid_race: 26 of 26 non-terminal comparisons: zero differing decoded fields and zero differing WRAM bytes at $0200+
findings.result_phase: 49 terminal seeds across all five arms: decoded fields identical until the reference's 0x16 restoration; first $0200+ byte difference 1-2 native frames before result-menu onset; raw 7E:009F (wTextPos) 0x84 phase {'(35, 34)': 48, '(36, 34)': 1} (native, reference); per-core onset/restore boundaries differ and are kept separate
